Module 1.title: Introduction to Engineering Drawing and Conic Sections
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Conics & Scales
  • Eccentricity ($e = VF / VD$): Ellipse ($e < 1$), Parabola ($e = 1$), Hyperbola ($e > 1$).
  • Representative Fraction (RF): $\text{RF} = \frac{\text{Dimension on drawing}}{\text{Actual physical dimension}}$. (Enlarging $\text{RF} > 1$, Full size $\text{RF} = 1$, Reducing $\text{RF} < 1$).
  • Special Curves: Involute of circle (unwinding string trajectory, basis of gear tooth profiles), Cycloid (rolling circle on straight line), Epicycloid / Hypocycloid (rolling circle outside/inside generating circle).
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Module 1 Reference: Graphics

BIS SP 46:2003 drawing standards, Title block conventions, First Angle ($Object$ between Observer and Plane) vs Third Angle projection.
Module 1.textbook_html:
1.1 Drawing Conventions and Geometric Conics

Engineering Graphics is the universal visual language of design engineers, standardizing 2D projections of 3D spatial geometry according to ISO and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).

Module 2.title: Orthographic Projections of Points, Lines and Traces
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Lines & Traces
  • Quadrant Conventions (First Angle): Point above HP ($y > 0$) appears above reference line $xy$ in Front View ($a'$); Point in front of VP ($x > 0$) appears below $xy$ in Top View ($a$).
  • True Length (TL) and Apparent Angles: True length $\theta$ with HP, $\phi$ with VP. Apparent angles $\alpha$ (elevation), $\beta$ (plan).
  • Rotating Line Method: Rotate elevation line about $a'$ to horizontal to project plan view true length, and vice versa. $TL = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}$.
  • Traces: Horizontal Trace (HT) where line intersects HP ($y=0$); Vertical Trace (VT) where line intersects VP ($x=0$).
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Module 2 Reference: Orthographic Projections

Trapezoid method and projection lines verification.
Module 2.textbook_html:
2.1 Spatial Kinematics of Straight Lines

Determining true lengths and inclinations of oblique piping and structural struts from orthogonal 2D projections.

Module 3.title: Projections of Regular Planes and Solids
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Planes & Solids
  • Projections of Planes: Three-stage method: (1) Assume plane parallel to reference plane; (2) Tilt to surface inclination; (3) Tilt edge/axis to secondary inclination.
  • Solids Classification: Polyhedra (Prisms, Pyramids, Tetrahedron, Octahedron) vs Solids of Revolution (Cylinder, Cone, Sphere).
  • Axis Inclined to One Plane: Draw initial position with axis perpendicular to plane of true base shape, then rotate front or top view.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Module 3 Reference: Solids

Auxiliary projection planes (AIP, AVP) for single-step true shape visualization.
Module 3.textbook_html:
3.1 Spatial Solid Orientation and Boundary Visibility

Determining visible solid contours and hidden dashed lines of machine castings.

Module 4.title: Sections of Solids and Development of Lateral Surfaces
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Sections & Developments
  • Section Plane: Cutting plane represented by long thin chain line with thick ends. Hatching lines drawn at $45^\circ$ spaced $1-3\,\text{mm}$.
  • True Shape of Section: Obtained by projecting onto an auxiliary plane parallel to the cutting section plane.
  • Development Methods:
    • Parallel Line Method (Prisms and Cylinders, perimeter $P = \pi D$ or $\sum b_i$).
    • Radial Line Method (Pyramids and Cones, sector angle $\theta = \frac{R}{L} \times 360^\circ$).
    • Triangulation Method (Transition pieces, hoppers, duct transitions).
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Module 4 Reference: Surface Development

Sheet metal fabrication layout for HVAC ducts and pressure vessel nozzles.
Module 4.textbook_html:
4.1 Sectioning and Sheet Metal Development

Module 5.title: Isometric Projection, Perspective Projection and CAD Overview
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Isometric & CAD
  • Isometric Scale: $\text{Isometric Length} = \sqrt{2/3} \times \text{True Length} \approx 0.816 \times TL$.
  • Isometric Axes: Three mutually perpendicular axes receding at $120^\circ$ to each other ($30^\circ$ to horizontal).
  • Four-Center Method: Used to draw isometric ellipses representing circles on isometric planes.
  • Perspective Projection: Visual ray method / Vanishing point method showing objects as seen by the human eye from station point $S$.
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Module 5 Reference: 3D Visualization

Introduction to parametric 3D CAD solid modeling (extrusion, revolution, loft, sweep).
Module 5.textbook_html:
